title: Further Explanation and Description
summary: We described objects that are important to us and explained why they matter. We learned words about value, like sentimental, priceless and worthless, and words for modern products, like state-of-the-art and user-friendly. We practised pausing to make our descriptions more interesting, and we reviewed the present perfect and present perfect continuous with 'How long?'.

grammar.title: Present perfect simple and continuous (How long? / How much? / How many?)
grammar.explain: Use the present perfect continuous (have been + -ing) to say how long an activity has continued until now. Use the present perfect simple (have + past participle) for results: how much or how many. State verbs like know, have, own and like usually stay in the simple form, even with 'How long?'.
grammar.explain_ar: نستخدم المضارع التام المستمر (have been + الفعل مع ing) لنقول منذ متى يستمر نشاط ما حتى الآن. ونستخدم المضارع التام البسيط (have + التصريف الثالث) للنتائج، أي للسؤال عن الكمية أو العدد (How much / How many). أما أفعال الحالة مثل know وhave وown وlike فتبقى عادة في الصيغة البسيطة حتى مع How long.
form: How long + have/has + subject + been + verb-ing? (an activity that continues)
How much / How many + have/has + subject + past participle? (a result)
State verbs (know, have, own, like, love, belong): have/has + past participle, even with How long
for + a period of time (for ages, for three hours) / since + a starting point (since 2019, since I was ten)

examples.en: How long have you known your wife? I've known her for ages.
examples.note: 'Know' is a state verb, so we don't say 'have been knowing'.

examples.en: I've had this watch since I was ten.
examples.note: 'Have' (own) is a state verb: present perfect simple.

examples.en: I've been learning English for two years.
examples.note: An activity that started in the past and is still going on.

examples.en: How many photos have you taken with your new phone?
examples.note: How many = a result, so present perfect simple.

examples.en: She's been using the same phone for five years.
examples.note: How long = the activity continues, so present perfect continuous.

mistakes.wrong: How long did you know your wife?
mistakes.right: How long have you known your wife?
mistakes.why: You still know her now, so use the present perfect, not the past simple.

mistakes.wrong: I've been knowing her for ages.
mistakes.why: 'Know' is a state verb. It doesn't usually take -ing.
With 'since' and 'for' about time until now, use the present perfect.
A number (how many) is a result: use the present perfect simple.

quiz.why: 'Know' is a state verb, and the friendship continues now: present perfect simple.

quiz.q: I ___ for this bus for forty minutes!
quiz.why: How long an activity has continued: present perfect continuous.

quiz.q: How many cups of coffee ___ today?
quiz.why: How many = a result: present perfect simple.

quiz.q: My grandmother has had this ring ___ 1975.
quiz.why: Use 'since' with a starting point in time.
Use 'for' with a period of time.

quiz.q: She looks tired. She ___ all morning.
quiz.why: A long activity up to now that explains the present result: present perfect continuous.
